So people keep asking me about the beaten-up UK compound-semi names, and IQE is the one where the *first* thing you do decides the whole call. Here's my read.

---

**TLDR:** Yes it was mispriced on 2026-02-27 — but as an *asset*, not as a business, and by 19p you'd already missed ~60% of the gap. Small speculative long into the refinancing binary; floor ~23p, and everything above that is an unfunded option on revenue IQE had never done. Not a core hold.

---

## Step 0a first — the ticker is a trap

Before any thesis: `analyze IQE` came back hollow. Bare `IQE` on the feed resolves to a `quoteType: ECNQUOTE` stub — frozen 52-week range `0.011 – 0.011`, `averageDailyVolume3Month: 0`, `tradeable: false`. That's a collision artifact, not a stock. Reason from it and you write "sub-penny, no data, pass" on a real £600m company. Discarded.

Real identity, cross-checked three ways:

| line | venue | price (2026-08-11) | MC |
|---|---|---|---|
| IQE.L | AIM (primary) | 46.015p | £612.5m |
| IQEPY | OTC Pink, ADR **1:25** | $15.60 | $830.6m |
| IQEPF | OTC Pink, ordinary | $0.621 | $826.6m |

Ratio check: 1,331,032,836 ÷ 53,241,313 = **25.00** ✓. Price check: 46.015p × 25 × 1.3499 = $15.53 vs $15.60 ✓. Both US lines track the primary. Good.

Second flag the harness threw: EV $686.47m vs MC+debt−cash $906.60m, a 32% gap. Reconciled — the feed built EV from the **GBP** market cap treated as USD (£612.5m + £76.0m net debt = £688.5m). The number's fine, the *currency label* is wrong. **Everything below is in GBP**, because revenue £97.3m is a GBP statement and mixing it with the ADR's USD market cap silently inverts every ratio.

Identity lines clear: Total assets £213.3m ≥ net PP&E £133.4 + cash £15.7 + inventory £18.7 = £167.8m ✓. Inventory ÷ COGS = 18.7/95.9 × 12 = **2.3 months** — normal for a wafer fab ✓.

**One gap I can't close:** EDGAR returned 403, and IQE is an AIM registrant anyway — its US lines are OTC Pink, so there is no 10-K to pull. Customer-concentration % and geographic split are therefore **unavailable, not zero**. That's load-bearing for a name with a history of consumer 3D-sensing concentration, so conviction drops a tier and it stays a monitoring item. Financing terms below are RNS-sourced and tagged; no script can load an AIM RNS.

## Archetype: Bottleneck by default — but it's a **Constraint**, and that's the whole discipline point

Hardware/materials → chokepoint unless positive evidence says otherwise. No drained profit pool, no standard IQE owns. So: chokepoint shape. But then the "can money solve this?" test:

MOCVD and MBE reactors are **buyable** — Aixtron and Veeco will sell you a fleet. Sumitomo, Landmark, IntelliEPI exist, and Coherent/Lumentum run epi in-house. What's actually scarce is the *qualified recipe on a customer's PDK*, which is 12–24 months of work — expensive, slow, and completely fundable. Physics doesn't stop a competitor here; time and money do.

That's a **Constraint, not a bottleneck** → tactical trade, never a multi-year marry-it thesis. Getting this wrong is how you hold a cyclical epi house for five years expecting monopoly economics.

Trace it to the bottom hop and it gets clearer:

InP epiwafer (IQE) -> **InP substrate** (AXT, Sumitomo Electric, JX) -> **4-inch InP single-crystal growth yield** — twinning and cracking at 4" is the un-fundable step, and 4" is what makes silicon-photonics volumes economic.

The real chokepoint is one layer *below* IQE. And the market knows: AXTI is $4.83bn today against IQE's $826.6m — 5.8x. Layer economics say the same thing, brutally:

| layer | name | gross margin | MC |
|---|---|---|---|
| substrate | AXTI | 32.2% | $4.83bn |
| **epi** | **IQE** | **1.4%** | **$0.83bn** |
| PIC / module | COHR / LITE | 37.0% / 40.8% | $63.6bn / $63.3bn |

IQE sits at the **margin-poorest step in its own chain**. So this is not a "scarce node out-multiples its dependents" trade — that read is just wrong here. It only works as an asset-value + operating-leverage trade.

Second-order allocation actor: **MACOM** — took ~11.5% equity plus long-term strategic supply agreements to lock epi supply. Except that's April 2026 (RNS). *On 2026-02-27* the allocation hunt was visible but uncontracted: the 12 Jan 2026 RNS said the Board was "negotiating non-binding offers for the Group as a whole in addition to separate bids for certain other Group assets." Non-binding is not funded.

## Structural position & forward revenue (as of the question date)

Revenue is melting, and had been for three years: **£167.5m (FY22) -> £115.3m (FY23) -> £118.0m (FY24) -> £97.3m (FY25)**. Gross profit £1.4m on £95.9m COGS. Operating income −£26.4m. Interest expense £7.3m — the interest bill alone is **5x the gross profit**.

But underneath: OCF flipped positive (−£2.9m -> **+£3.7m**), FCF improved (−£17.7m -> −£4.6m), capex starved to £8.4m from £17.9m. They stopped bleeding and started running the installed fleet. And the 12 Jan RNS flagged ~£97m FY25 revenue at "adjusted EBITDA at least £2.0m," upper end of range, with a strong Q1 order book — photonics/AI + defence funding pulled forward.

Price on 2026-02-27: **19.00p**, after 10.38p on Feb 19 -> 16.02p -> 20.00p on Feb 26. I could not date the specific late-Feb catalyst with my tools — marking it UNCONFIRMED; the deterministic price record is what I'm working from.

## The lens — asset-value turnaround, forked, both legs run

Melting income statement + hard redeployable plant = replacement cost, not EV/Rev, not gross margin. The 1.4% GM is the *source* of the mispricing, not the disqualifier.

Inputs (FY25, 2025-12-31): gross PP&E £300.8m · net PP&E £133.4m · accum. dep. −£167.4m · tangible book £72.4m · goodwill £0.0 (written off) · cash £15.7m · total debt £91.7m (current £47.1m, LT £0.0m → ~£44.6m is IFRS-16 lease) · shares 978,274,122.

`Lens (floor): replacement-cost — EV £261.9m (MC 978.27m sh × 19.00p = £185.9m + net debt £76.0m) ÷ gross PP&E £300.8m = 0.87x`

On financial debt only (£47.1m + £0.0m − £15.7m = **£31.4m** — independently corroborated by the reported "adjusted net debt £31.5m", RNS): £217.3m ÷ £300.8m = **0.72x**.

So at 19p you bought the installed fleet for 72–87p on the pound of historical cost, and got twenty years of qualification and recipe learning — which is *nowhere* on the balance sheet — for free.

Now the other leg. The FY22→FY25 bridge gives me the drop-through: revenue −£70.2m, COGS −£45.2m → incremental gross margin **(70.2−45.2)/70.2 = 35.6%** (DEDUCED from the revenue/COGS bridge, ~64% of COGS is fixed). Opex = £1.4m GP − (−£26.4m) = £27.8m.

`Lens (upside): operating-leverage — (£167.5m − £97.3m) × 35% + £1.4m GP − £27.8m opex + £24.2m D&A = £22.3m EBITDA -> EV £261.9m ÷ £22.3m = 11.7x`

And here's where the two legs fight, and the answer isn't the one I wanted:

**At 19p the market was already paying ~12x a full round-trip to the 2022 peak.** Revenue back to £167.5m — the best year IQE ever had, on the same asset base — gets you to roughly spot. Every pound above ~23p required IQE to do revenue it had **never done**.

Run the band out:
- Floor, EV = 1.0x gross PP&E: (£300.8m − £76.0m) ÷ 978.27m = **23.0p** (27.5p if you don't charge the leases)
- £200m revenue, 12x: EBITDA 0.35×200 − 36.3 = £33.7m → (£404.4m − £76.0m) ÷ 978.27m = **33.6p**
- £250m revenue, 12x: EBITDA £51.2m → (£614.4m − £76.0m) ÷ 978.27m = **55.0p**

vs 19.00p spot. ADR equivalents at Feb FX 1.3491: $7.76 / $11.33 / $18.55 vs $6.50.

## Price-extreme check — I ran the bearish fade first, and it failed

On 2026-02-27 IQE sat at the **93.4th percentile of its 52-week range**, **+131.1% over the 200-day**, **3.89x off the 4.88p low**. Textbook "you've missed it, don't chase."

So prove the math before saying it. At the 4.88p low, EV was £48.9m + £76.0m = £124.9m = **0.42x gross PP&E** — the market was pricing liquidation. At 19p it's 0.87x. That 4x move re-rated the name from *bankruptcy* to *below-replacement-cost going concern*. It did **not** re-rate it to a recovery multiple.

So the "don't chase" call is wrong for the reason people think it's right — but the price-extreme still bites, because what got removed was a *discount*, and it got removed on **non-binding offer newsflow, not contracted capital**. The market pre-priced an outcome nobody had signed.

## Winner gates — 1 pass, 1 partial, 3 fails, 1 binary

1. **Monetization — FAIL.** 1.4% gross margin. Critical to the chain, money not in the door. Volume-fixable, but unfixed.
2. **Pricing realization — FAIL.** Three years of falling revenue at ~zero GM. Merchant epi is a price-taker.
3. **Survival to the ramp — CONDITIONAL, and it's the binary.** £47.1m current debt vs £15.7m cash. The Feb-2025 convertible notes ran an initial 12-month term (RNS) — i.e. maturing *on* the question date — plus a $35m HSBC RCF. Interest coverage −4.09x.
4. **TAM expansion — PASS.** InP/photonics is genuine migration off the melting 3D-sensing base.
5. **Allocation control — FAIL as of 27 Feb** (uncontracted). Flips in April.
6. **Demand breadth — PARTIAL, unverifiable.** Photonics + wireless + defence is real breadth, but customer concentration % is unavailable (no SEC filing).

That's not a winner clear. It's a cheap asset attached to a business that doesn't clear the bar — which is a real thing that exists, and it's why sizing matters more than direction here.

**Cycle stage: 2/3 boundary.** Reported annual revenue still *down*; OCF turned, capex starved, order book firming. Magnitude peaks exactly here and so does uncertainty.

**Priced in at 19p:** removal of the liquidation discount; the *existence* of AI-optics InP demand.
**Not priced in:** a funded balance sheet; the 35% drop-through on recovered volume; a strategic customer taking equity plus a supply agreement.
The gap between those two lists is the trade.

**Downsides:**
- **The refinancing was an unresolved binary landing inside ~90 days.** A lowball takeout or a deeply discounted rescue transfers the asset value away from you at 19p. *Not priced in* — the market was pricing the good outcome.
- **The dilution actually came.** Shares 978.3m -> 1,331.0m, **+36%**. Anyone modelling per-share value off 978m was wrong within eight weeks. *Not priced in.*
- **IQE is the margin-poorest layer in its own chain** (1.4% GM vs AXTI 32.2%). The scarce node is InP crystal growth, one hop down. *Structural, addressed by sizing small — not by the thesis.*
- **The vehicle is bad.** Both US lines are OTC Pink, no listed options, IQEPY float 25.75m of 53.24m ADRs, institutional holdings read 0.0 with a single 57-share holder (that's a null, not a signal). Short interest unavailable. So with beta 2.208 after a +93% week, IV was surely fat — and there's **no CSP or LEAP to harvest it with**. *Addressed only by position size.*

**Falsifier — breaks if the built fleet fails to convert recovering InP volume into gross margin.** Specifically: revenue recovers but incremental GM lands materially below the ~35% the FY22→FY25 bridge implies (permanently inflated fixed base, or Sumitomo/in-house epi competing the price away). Secondary: the refinancing resolves at a price that transfers the asset to someone else.

## Rating

**Speculative BUY, small — 1–2% sizing, tactical, not a core hold.** Conviction **medium-low**, capped by three things: unverifiable customer concentration, an unproven funding gate, and the constraint-not-bottleneck classification.

- PT band as of 2026-02-27: **23p floor / 34p base / 55p bull** (IQEPY ~$7.76 / $11.33 / $18.55), 9–18 months.
- Vehicle: **shares only, on IQEPY** (the ADR — better price granularity than IQEPF at $0.62, same exposure). No options exist. Scale in; don't take it in one clip after a 93%-of-range week.
- Kill: a rescue raise priced materially below 19p, or a takeout at a discount to the 23p replacement floor.

## What actually happened — flagged, all of this postdates 2026-02-27

27–28 April 2026: strategic review concluded with an **£81m package at 19.8p** — within 4% of the question-date price. MACOM put in £45m (£30m equity + £15m zero-coupon secured convertible, ~11.5%), £22.8m noteholder reinvestment, £13m placing/retail; proceeds repaid the HSBC RCF and redeemed the notes. Long-term supply agreements alongside. June: multi-year Tower Semiconductor InP epiwafer supply deal. July: FY26 guidance raised to >30% growth, H1 ≥£64m, low-teens £m adjusted EBITDA. Price 19.00p -> 46.015p (**+142%**), 2026 closing high 63.0p. (RNS/press-sourced; not code-loadable.)

So the structure of the call held — the mispricing was real and the resolution mechanism was the refinancing, exactly where the risk sat. R4 also got vindicated in the direction that matters: what re-rated the name was *third-party contract capital* (a customer writing an equity check and signing offtake), not the company minting stock into its own story.

But be honest about the entry: the asset-value gap was ~21% to floor at 19p, and the +142% came from the *story* leg — the bit you could not underwrite on 27 Feb. That's a good outcome partly for a reason the Feb-27 evidence didn't support.

That's an **Evolution** trigger, not a story: the willingness-to-pay is set by the cost of scrapping a packaged accelerator+HBM stack, not by the price of the burn-in.
